//: The hand-written part of the generated Python layer (scripts/python-api.mjs): how TypeScript types become Python types and NumPy arrays, and what only Python has. Everything else comes from the TypeScript entry points and their TSDoc.

symcrys.docstring:
symcrys: crystallographic symmetry calculations, from Python.

A thin layer over the TypeScript library symcrys of the same version, which runs in an embedded
JavaScript engine (quickjs-ng). Every function here calls the function of the same name in the
library (camelCase there, snake_case here) and returns its result as plain Python data, matrices
and vectors as NumPy arrays, records as dicts typed by the TypedDicts of the module (rules in
``symcrys._convert``). The conventions, frames and their
sources are documented once, for both languages: https://manganite.github.io/symcrys/conventions.html

This module is the crystallographic API: the 32 crystal classes, without time reversal. The
magnetic point groups, time-odd tensors and operations with time reversal are in
``symcrys.magnetic``, under the same function names; there ``"32"`` is the white group, and a
crystal without magnetic order has the grey group of its class (quartz: ``"321'"``). A question
that involves time reversal raises ``SymcrysError`` here (docs/conventions.md, "Two entry points").
The plane groups and plane point groups are in ``symcrys.plane``.

Each call costs about a millisecond or more (the forms of rank-4 tensors up to a few tenths of a
second); fetch operations or forms once and compute with NumPy, rather than calling in a loop.

symcrys.magnetic.docstring:
symcrys.magnetic: the magnetic API, for the 122 magnetic point groups, with time reversal.

The functions have the names they have in ``symcrys``, the crystallographic API; the module decides
which reading a key has. Here a key of type ``'I'`` (``"32"``) is a white (colourless) group: the
symmetry of a magnetically ordered crystal in which time reversal does not occur at all. A crystal
without magnetic order has the grey group of its class (quartz: ``"321'"``), which allows no
time-odd property. Operations carry ``time_reversal``, a tensor specification ``time_parity``
(docs/conventions.md, "Two entry points").

symcrys.plane.docstring:
symcrys.plane: the plane API, for the 17 plane groups and the 10 plane point groups.

Coordinates and operations are in the lattice basis (a, b), as ITA gives them for the plane
groups. Keys are ITA's symbols: ``"p2mg"``, ``"c2mm"`` for the plane groups,
``"2mm"``, ``"3m"`` for the plane point groups. A matrix is an int64 array of shape (2, 2), a
translation, a point and a vertex float64 arrays of shape (2,); a direction of a
line is an int64 array of shape (2,) (docs/conventions.md, "Plane groups").

types.//: TypeScript type names with a fixed Python reading: 'str' for keys, an array shape for vectors and matrices, 'int' for an integer type.

literals.//: Literal types whose values are the keys of a constant of the entry point.

arrays.//: The dtype of an array of numbers in a result, by the name of its field: float64 or int64. A field of arrays not listed is an error of the generator. symcrys.plane has its own list, since there `direction` is a lattice direction.

shapes.//: The shape of an array field where the nested lists may be empty (-1: any length).

numbers.//: Number fields and option properties by name: int or float.

functions.//: What a function's TypeScript type does not say: the dtype of an array it returns, the keys an operation must have, an argument converted otherwise; mappings: object parameters passed as one mapping rather than as their fields; operationKeys, bare and listOf may be given per module (siteSymmetryOf and orbitOf do not depend on time reversal, docs/conventions.md).

operations.//: The record of arrays that stands for a list of operations in Python: the TypeScript record of one operation, and per field its dtype and the shape of one entry. `bare`: the field a bare array of matrices (n, 3, 3) is read as; none in symcrys.magnetic (it does not say whether an operation carries time reversal) and symcrys.plane (no Cartesian matrices).

symcrys.doc: The operations of a point group as arrays, one row per operation, in the order of ``operations``: what ``operations``, ``generators`` and ``residual_operations`` return, and what every function that takes operations accepts, beside a list of dicts ``{"cartesian"}`` and an array of Cartesian matrices of shape (n, 3, 3). Frozen, its arrays read-only; ``len(ops)`` is the number of operations.

symcrys.magnetic.doc: The operations of a magnetic point group as arrays, one row per operation, in the order of ``operations``: what ``operations``, ``generators`` and ``residual_operations`` return, and what every function that takes operations accepts, beside a list of dicts ``{"cartesian", "time_reversal"}``. An array of matrices alone is refused here, since it does not say which operations carry time reversal. Frozen, its arrays read-only; ``len(ops)`` is the number of operations.

symcrys.plane.doc: The operations of a plane group or plane point group as arrays, one row per operation, in the order of ``operations``: what ``operations`` and ``generators`` return, and what ``describe_operations_of`` accepts, beside a list of dicts ``{"matrix", "translation"}``. Frozen, its arrays read-only; ``len(ops)`` is the number of operations.

transformed.//: The record of arrays for the operations of a change of coordinates in Python, as for "operations".

symcrys.doc: The operations of ``change_of_coordinates`` in the new coordinate system as arrays, one row per operation, in the order given: each a matrix W′ and a translation w′. Frozen, its arrays read-only; ``len(ops)`` is the number of operations; they can be passed back to ``change_of_coordinates``.

symcrys.magnetic.doc: The operations of ``change_of_coordinates`` in the new coordinate system as arrays, one row per operation, in the order given: each a matrix W′ and a translation w′. Frozen, its arrays read-only; ``len(ops)`` is the number of operations; they can be passed back to ``change_of_coordinates``.
